records.title: Introduction to the American Legal System
records.header: T LAW 150 Introduction to the American Legal System (5) SSc
records.text: T LAW 150 Introduction to the American Legal System (5) SSc Provides an introduction to the American legal system, and examines how judicial processes relate to American politics. Describes the organization of state and federal courts; judicial selection and elections; and the functioning of criminal, civil, and appellate courts, including the U.S. Supreme Court.

records.title: Pre-Law Seminar
records.header: T LAW 200 Pre-Law Seminar (2)
records.text: T LAW 200 Pre-Law Seminar (2) Teaches students about the practice of law, the law school admissions process, and legal careers. Students will gain practical insight, engage in community-based learning where appropriate/possible, and have the opportunity to interact with legal professionals. Credit/no-credit only.

records.title: Introduction to International Organizations
records.header: T LAW 215 Introduction to International Organizations (5) SSc
records.text: T LAW 215 Introduction to International Organizations (5) SSc Explores historical, theoretical, and empirical aspects of the United Nations, its specialized agencies, and other international organizations, both governmental and nongovernmental. Course equivalent to: POL S 328.

records.title: Street Law
records.header: T LAW 300 Street Law (2, max. 4) SSc
records.text: T LAW 300 Street Law (2, max. 4) SSc Explore an area of law that interests the students and to then communicate what they have learned to their local community. Specific legal issues explored will depend on their interests, and will change each time the course is offered. Credit/no-credit only.

records.title: American Constitutional Law: Institutional Powers and Constraints
records.header: T LAW 320 American Constitutional Law: Institutional Powers and Constraints (5) SSc
records.text: T LAW 320 American Constitutional Law: Institutional Powers and Constraints (5) SSc Explores the role of the Supreme Court in interpreting the United States Constitution. Covers the role of the federal government in relationship with the states, judicial review, the separation of powers, and economic due process.

records.title: Washington Environmental Law
records.header: T LAW 339 Washington Environmental Law (5)
records.text: T LAW 339 Washington Environmental Law (5) Examines Washington State environmental statutes through reading, writing, and discussion of regulations and case studies. Takes a case law approach to evaluate laws in biological conservation, energy, land use, mineral rights, air and water quality, and other complex environmental arenas, and how Washington courts have interpreted such laws.

records.title: Violence and the Law
records.header: T LAW 345 Violence and the Law (5) SSc, DIV
records.text: T LAW 345 Violence and the Law (5) SSc, DIV Focuses on violence and law, particularly as to how law defines, promotes, and responds to violence. It will orient students to social theories of violence through which the relationship between violence and law can be explored and survey a few topics to explore the boundaries of private - public and legitimized - delegitimized violences to develop a critical understanding of how law interacts with violence. Course overlaps with: LSJ 375/SOC 372.

records.title: Gender and Law
records.header: T LAW 348 Gender and Law (5) SSc, DIV
records.text: T LAW 348 Gender and Law (5) SSc, DIV Studies the way gender norms influence legal processes and the role of the law in gendered social change. Explores some of the practical strategies men and women may employ in order to negotiate and use gendered constraints to their advantage.

records.title: American Constitutional Law: Rights and Liberties
records.header: T LAW 361 American Constitutional Law: Rights and Liberties (5) SSc
records.text: T LAW 361 American Constitutional Law: Rights and Liberties (5) SSc Explores the role of the United States Supreme Court in interpreting the Bill of Rights. Covers topics such as freedom of speech and religion, privacy, equal protection, and criminal due process. Course equivalent to: POL S 361/LSJ 361.

records.title: Law in Society
records.header: T LAW 363 Law in Society (5) SSc
records.text: T LAW 363 Law in Society (5) SSc Inquiry into how law matters in social practice. Examines general theories of law, the workings of legal institutions, and the character of legally constituted practices and relationships in diverse terrains of social life. Course equivalent to: POL S 363/LSJ 363.

records.title: Comparative Law and Courts
records.header: T LAW 367 Comparative Law and Courts (5) SSc
records.text: T LAW 367 Comparative Law and Courts (5) SSc Introduces comparative judicial politics, focusing on the relationship between law and politics in cross-national perspective, as well as the function of supranational and international legal entities in the international system.

records.title: History of Mass Incarceration in the United States
records.header: T LAW 380 History of Mass Incarceration in the United States (5) SSc
records.text: T LAW 380 History of Mass Incarceration in the United States (5) SSc Explores the rise of mass incarceration in the United States across economic, legal, political, and social terrains. Situates mass incarceration in a longer history of U.S. punishment systems. Includes a sub-focus on how these issues have manifested in Washington state. Course overlaps with: BIS 336.

records.title: International Humanitarian Law
records.header: T LAW 422 International Humanitarian Law (5) SSc
records.text: T LAW 422 International Humanitarian Law (5) SSc Investigates International Humanitarian Law (sometimes called the Law of Armed Conflict), the field concerned with rules developed by civilized nations to protect the victims of armed conflict, including the Geneva Conventions. Case studies include the conflict between Israel and the Palestinians, as well as developments in Afghanistan and Iraq. Course equivalent to: JSIS A 465.

records.header: T LAW 423 International Law (5) SSc
records.text: T LAW 423 International Law (5) SSc Origin and present status of efforts to make rules of conduct for sovereign states; simulation of a treaty-drafting conference, with students playing roles of legal advisers to foreign governments. Course equivalent to: POL S 347/LSJ 347.

records.title: The Politics and Law of International Human Rights
records.header: T LAW 424 The Politics and Law of International Human Rights (5) SSc
records.text: T LAW 424 The Politics and Law of International Human Rights (5) SSc Studies the international human rights movement in its legal and political context. Focus on institutions which influence, enable, and constrain the international promotion of human rights. Course overlaps with: POL S 368/LSJ 320.

records.title: Rights of Nature
records.header: T LAW 425 Rights of Nature (5) SSc
records.text: T LAW 425 Rights of Nature (5) SSc Explores how human rights law is used to promote the rights of nature and the rights of more-than-human beings. Examines cases decided by courts in various jurisdictions across the world, with a primary emphasis on Latin-American and international courts.

records.title: Federal Environmental Law
records.header: T LAW 438 Federal Environmental Law (5) SSc
records.text: T LAW 438 Federal Environmental Law (5) SSc Examines the historical and policy framework of major environmental laws and regulations. Takes a case law approach to evaluate laws in biological conservation, energy, land use, mineral rights, air and water quality, and other complex environmental arenas, and how courts (primarily in the United States) have interpreted such laws.

records.title: Race, Ethnicity, and the Law
records.header: T LAW 452 Race, Ethnicity, and the Law (5) SSc, DIV
records.text: T LAW 452 Race, Ethnicity, and the Law (5) SSc, DIV Examines the 20th century evolution of equal protection and due process. Particular focus placed upon the case law, its societal context, and its impact upon persons of color.

records.title: Law and Public Policy in the United States
records.header: T LAW 465 Law and Public Policy in the United States (5) SSc
records.text: T LAW 465 Law and Public Policy in the United States (5) SSc Relationship between law and public policy, with particular attention to problems of social, economic, and political change. Considers legal and constitutional processes as they relate to such problems of public policy as race relations, the environment, and the economy. Course equivalent to: POL S 465.

records.title: Field Work in Law and Policy
records.header: T LAW 486 Field Work in Law and Policy (5) SSc
records.text: T LAW 486 Field Work in Law and Policy (5) SSc Applies work in policy and law. Student engage in fieldwork and research to examine a policy issue in the community. Working collaboratively with community members and lawmakers, students propose legislation, and publicly present recommendations to lawmakers. Prerequisite: either TPOL S 202, TPOL S 305, or TPOL S 382.
